question: Who was the 7th president of the United States?
fact: Andrew Jackson served two terms, from 1829 to 1837.
source: Miller Center, University of Virginia: presidential profile, Andrew Jackson (millercenter.org/president/jackson)

question: Who became president after Abraham Lincoln was assassinated?
fact: Vice President Andrew Johnson took over on April 15, 1865, the day Lincoln died.
source: Miller Center, University of Virginia: presidential profile, Andrew Johnson (millercenter.org/president/johnson)

question: Grover Cleveland served two non-consecutive terms. Which two numbers does he hold in the count of presidents?
fact: Benjamin Harrison, the 23rd president, served between Cleveland's two terms.
source: White House Historical Association: Grover Cleveland (whitehouse.gov/about-the-white-house/presidents/grover-cleveland)

question: Which president issued the Emancipation Proclamation?
fact: The proclamation, effective January 1, 1863, declared enslaved people in Confederate-held territory to be free.

question: Which president completed the Louisiana Purchase in 1803?
fact: The purchase from France roughly doubled the size of the United States.

question: Which president launched the New Deal in response to the Great Depression?
fact: The New Deal programs began in 1933, early in Franklin D. Roosevelt's first term.
source: Miller Center, University of Virginia: presidential profile, Franklin D. Roosevelt (millercenter.org/president/fdroosevelt)

question: Which vice president became president when William McKinley died in 1901?
fact: McKinley died on September 14, 1901, eight days after being shot, and Roosevelt was sworn in as president.
source: Miller Center, University of Virginia: presidential profile, Theodore Roosevelt (millercenter.org/president/roosevelt)

question: Which president later served as Chief Justice of the United States?
fact: William Howard Taft was president from 1909 to 1913 and Chief Justice from 1921 to 1930.
source: Supreme Court of the United States: Chief Justices, William Howard Taft (supremecourt.gov)

question: In which state was Ronald Reagan born?
fact: Reagan was born in Tampico, Illinois, in 1911, and later served as governor of California.
source: Ronald Reagan Presidential Library and Museum: biography (reaganlibrary.gov)

question: Which president said in his 1961 inaugural address, "Ask not what your country can do for you — ask what you can do for your country"?
fact: Kennedy delivered the line at his inauguration on January 20, 1961.
source: John F. Kennedy Presidential Library and Museum: Inaugural Address, January 20, 1961 (jfklibrary.org)

question: Who was the first president to live in the White House?
fact: John Adams moved in in November 1800, while the building was still unfinished.
source: White House Historical Association: John Adams and the White House (whitehousehistory.org)

question: Who was the first president born after the Declaration of Independence?
fact: Martin Van Buren, the 8th president, was born in Kinderhook, New York, in 1782.
source: Miller Center, University of Virginia: presidential profile, Martin Van Buren (millercenter.org/president/vanburen)
